subject: health
title: Guided practice: stress signals and triggers
essentialQuestion: How can I manage strong feelings and know when to reach for support?
materials: cards or paper for a coping toolkit
optional timer for a calming practice
keyPoints: Stress shows up in the body — headaches, stomach aches, tight muscles, disturbed sleep.
It shows up in behaviour too — snapping, avoiding, rushing, or going quiet.
A trigger is the situation that sets it off; noticing patterns lets you plan ahead.
Some stress before a challenge is normal and can help you focus.
privacySafeScenario: Every Sunday evening one learner gets a stomach ache that clears by Monday afternoon. What might the trigger be, and how could you check?
studentTask: The learner applies what they learned about stress signals and triggers to a new fictional situation and records the choice plus the reason behind it.
knowledgeCheck: Using the practice situation, say what the safest or healthiest next step is and why.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about stress signals and triggers.
The learner gives a reason, an example, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
adaptationChoices: Coping strategies may be movement-based, still, sensory, verbal, or silent, and each learner selects strategies their body and setting allow. Scenario responses may be pointed to, chosen from options, drawn, spoken, or written.
extensionChallenge: Apply what you learned about stress signals and triggers under a new constraint, compare two reasonable approaches, or teach the idea to a family member with an original fictional example.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, signed, drawn, or pointed responses; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety, health, or mental-health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.

optionalReflection.prompt: With a guardian, agree one signal you can use at home that means "I need a few minutes". This is optional. No purchase, account creation, photograph, measurement, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
